projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

This matters because it confirms the home is occupied despite the cameras, but warrants a quick verification to ensure camera functionality and rule out sensor inflation.

The sustained presence of 16–20 devices alongside zero camera motion over four hours strongly indicates the household is stationary in a camera-blind area rather than away, but warrants a quick camera health check given the typical activity levels of two kids and two high-energy dogs.

The steady drop in connected devices (22 to 16) paired with zero camera motion over four hours strongly suggests the entire household is currently away from home, likely on a Saturday outing. The recent stabilization in device count indicates they are stationary nearby rather than in transit, confirming the house is safely empty for security and automation purposes.

The sharp decline in connected devices (11:57–12:19) combined with zero camera motion over four hours strongly suggests the household has either left the property or moved to a non-monitored outdoor area; verifying camera functionality and sending a quick check-in is recommended to rule out equipment issues or an unexpected absence.

The gradual drop in connected devices from 22 to 19 over three hours, paired with zero camera motion, suggests devices are likely powering down or drifting out of Wi-Fi range rather than people leaving the house. This warrants a quick check to ensure cameras are active and not stuck in night mode or offline.

The presence count increase to 22 at 06:41 aligns with the children waking up, while the drop to 21 at 09:04 suggests a departure; the absence of corresponding camera activity indicates they likely left via an unmonitored entry or simply disconnected from Wi-Fi, which is consistent with a normal Saturday morning routine.

The stable device count (21-22), zero camera motion, and Steve’s continuous sleep tracking confirm the entire household is in a deep, uninterrupted sleep cycle. Steve’s short sleep duration is offset by his stable HR/HRV and lack of wake indicators, suggesting he is resting effectively rather than experiencing fragmented sleep, so no immediate action is required.

The stable device count and zero camera motion confirm the household remains asleep, while Steve’s normal resting heart rate and strong HRV despite only 2.09h of sleep indicate his body is still recovering well; this suggests a relaxed morning is sufficient rather than concern over acute sleep deprivation.
